entries.note: CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-31T05:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2, as it may be obscured by the pylon or too faint to view clearly. The source of this event is an eruption from former AR 14561 (S11W140) beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T04:30Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195. Brightening near the region and dimming extending Northward can be seen in association with this eruption, possibly suggesting a Northern deflection.

Very minor and faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs and not seen in STEREO A COR2. Its source is a very minor eruption from the former AR 14561 (S10W130) starting ~2026-10-30T11:25Z as seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. AR 14561 rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-10-27.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption with liftoff starting around 2026-10-29T07:36Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The footpoints extend from about S20W20 to S10W50. Post eruptive dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 with an opening of field lines seen over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery.

Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, also very faintly observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and difficult to resolve, becoming more defined as it travels further into each coronagraph's field-of-view. The source is likely former AR 14561, located around S10W95 at this time. There is no distinct, clean eruption associated with this front, but rather slow field line movement and brightening from this region of the disk in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-10-28T09:46Z, also observed as some field line movement and brightening near AR 14561 in STEREO A EUVI 195.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement on/near the high latitude N limb around 2026-10-27T22:31Z in SDO AIA 171, or far-sided and unobserved.
Faint CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source location is not found in available EUV imagery.

Narrow CME visible to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and the NE in STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be a faint filament eruption best seen starting around 2026-10-27T02:16Z in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. Post-eruption dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193 centered around N40E20.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.  This event was also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 after a downlink data gap backfilled and was seen in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-10-26T20:38Z to 2026-10-27T02:23Z. The source is a large filament eruption visible near the eastern limb which begins to lift off around 2026-10-26T20:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 imagery. The filament may extend as far as longitude E50 to beyond the east limb. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery despite data availability, likely because it is directed towards the spacecraft and therefore occulted by the coronagraph. The source is related to an eruption and C2.8 flare from Active Region 14561 (S12W77) starting around 2026-10-26T18:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME follows the more faint CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this front and CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z. For this front, the eruptive source is likely an area of dimming and field line movement centered ~S05W80 in the vicinity of AR 14561, observed in SDO AIA 171/195, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304, starting around 2026-10-26T09:10Z. This follows separate field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z ~S09W72, likely responsible for preceding CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z.

CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME precedes and partially overlapped by the larger CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this front and CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z. For this front, the eruptive source is likely field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193, and on-disk brightening in SDO AIA 304 and STEREO A EUVI 304, starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z and centered around S09W72. Also associated with a C1.9 flare peaking at 2026-10-26T08:38Z, observed in SDO AIA 131.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75) seen best in SDO AIA 131/193/304 imagery starting around 2026-10-26T01:30Z.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to an opening of field lines visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2026-10-25T23:55Z, likely associated with a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75).

Faint CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely far-sided over the east limb, potentially observed as field line movement in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-25T23:06Z.

CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-25T19:24Z. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen in SDO AIA 304 located at approx. S10W60, beginning at approx. 2026-10-25T18:42Z. Field line opening is also seen in SDO AIA 171/193.

Faint CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. It is likely not observed in STEREO A COR2, but the NW quadrant of COR2 imagery is overlapped with prior CME activity and may obscure this front. The source is likely far-sided, due to the lack of any on-disk EUV observations corresponding to this front time.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, starting very slow. It is either not yet seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-10-25T10:09Z or too faint to resolve the leading edge. The source appears to be a mix of continued slow field line movement over the E limb following CME 2026-10-25T03:12Z, whose eruption began around 2026-10-25T02:09Z in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304, and/or further field line movement in GOES SUVI 171/284 starting around 2026-10-25T04:30Z.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source is wide field line movement over the E limb starting around 2026-10-25T02:09Z in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304; the prominence on the limb jostles in SDO AIA 304/GOES SUVI 304  but does not cleanly erupt. Preceeded by and overtakes a faint leading edge starting at 2026-10-25T01:48Z measuring ~173 km/s, from field line movement over the NE limb ~2026-10-25T00:58Z in GOES SUVI 284 prior to the main eruption. Followed by and overlaps with a streamer blowout starting around 2026-10-25T05:00Z.

Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided, observed in GOES SUVI 284 as field line movement beyond the W limb around 2026-10-24T22:06Z, and may be directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 as brightening in the vicinity of former AR 14551 at 2026-10-24T20:45Z.

Relatively narrow CME to the NNW seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3 because of poor image quality. It is covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2 so far. The source is likely the opening/movement of field lines and possibly small ejecta seen on/beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171/131/304 after 2026-10-24T21:12Z.
A narrow jet-like CME seen to the WSW in all three coronagraphs. No source has been found for this jet-like feature in the EUV imagery.
